h1: JungleMind — AI & SaaS Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product, captured at 1920x1422 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product — fluid type, 70ms transitions, #5C5C5C base and cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) easing.
about: This is the landing page from JungleMind, published with the brief that produced it rather than as a screenshot. The palette is #5C5C5C underneath and #111111 for the type, set in Poppins. The entry names the stack that produced the page (vanilla JS) rather than hiding it. Motion is confined to 70ms transitions, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) and a looping video bed. Keep it open while you write: the 36,531-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: Top row: wordmark, links, one action
layout.body: The bar overlays the landing page instead of pushing it down, so the composition keeps the full height of the first screen. Below 340px the links collapse instead of wrapping onto a second line. If your own page has more sections, group them rather than widening the bar.

layout.title: Video at the bottom layer
layout.body: The media is one 6.9s clip cropped to cover the 1920x1422 frame, so it never letterboxes at any width. A poster frame at 1920x1422 holds the composition when autoplay is unavailable, so the layout never collapses.

layout.title: The scale steps down hard
layout.body: The face is quoted with its sizes (Poppins across 12–25px), which is what makes the type portable between builds. Tracking tightens as the size grows, which is why the display line holds together across 12–25px.

layout.title: Links before the action
layout.body: The bar is a handful of elements, so it rebuilds without a component library. The reference was captured at 1920x1422.

motion.title: Hover where it means something
motion.body: Feedback is limited to hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card, which is what keeps a dense first screen from feeling busy. Feedback is limited to the controls, so the composition stays still around them. Keep the pointer effects on the controls.

motion.title: It respects reduced-motion
motion.body: Reduced motion is specified rather than bolted on: with it on, the entrance and the loop stops and the composition holds its final state. The branch is part of the brief rather than an afterthought. Test the page with motion disabled.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over #5C5C5C, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.

fonts.name: Poppins
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

notes: Panel corners reuse the radius list in the brief (9px and 2px), so the grid needs no separate treatment.
The clip is one asset at 1920x1422 and a 6.9s loop, so the composition has a single media dependency.
Nothing sits between the type and the 1920x1422 clip, so a replacement has to work under the copy directly.

customize: Replace the video with a still at 1920x1422 if the 6.9s loop is too heavy for the page you are shipping.
Retime the entrance to taste. 70ms with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) is what the reference uses.
Swap the clip for your own footage at 1920x1422 or wider, keep it muted, and match the 6.9s loop point.
Retime the entrance to your own 70ms, but keep cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) as the curve, because the easing is what reads as this design.

editorial.title: What an AI or SaaS product gains here
editorial.body: 36,531 characters of brief produce one screen with no filler. The values in it are explicit (type from 12px to 25px and 100vh sections), which is why the composition still reads when the words change. It gives a SaaS reader the shortest honest route to the offer.

editorial.title: Reading JungleMind as a spec
editorial.body: The brief is a specification. It states type from 12px to 25px, 100vh sections, 9px corners, 16px spacing steps and 70ms transitions, and it names the media frame at 1920x1422 before anything is designed around it. Nothing in this landing page depends on a default.

editorial.title: How the landing page reflows
editorial.body: Test this landing page at 1920x1422 and then at phone width: the same order holds, with the type is clamped between 12px and 25px, the layout shifts at 340px and the section is held at 100vh. A squeeze would have been cheaper and would not hold.

steps: Pin the reference measurements before you restyle anything: type from 12px to 25px, 100vh sections and 9px corners.
Check your build against the reference measurements: type from 12px to 25px, 100vh sections and 9px corners.
Keep the measurements the brief spells out: type from 12px to 25px, 100vh sections and 9px corners.
Copy type from 12px to 25px, 100vh sections and 9px corners into your own brief before you rewrite anything else.
Rebuild the motion last and keep the 70ms entrance; the hover and scroll states come after it.

faq.question: What does the brief behind JungleMind actually contain?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 36,531 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: Do I need vanilla JS to rebuild JungleMind?
faq.answer: JungleMind was built in vanilla JS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: How much of JungleMind is animated?
faq.answer: The motion is specified at the same level of detail as the layout: state changes settle in the 70ms range using cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). Port the composition first and the timings second, because they are easier to match once the layout holds.

audience: Founders who brief an agency will use the 1920x1422 frame as the acceptance test for the first round.
Designers who need the numbers first: type from 12px to 25px and 100vh sections, all of it quoted from the brief.
Made for content leads rewriting a landing page whose headline has to stay as long as JungleMind's.
